abstract: As the principle immune cell of the central nervous system (CNS), microglia have been extensively studied throughout development and in a wide range of disease states. Of special focus have been their morphological features such as branching complexity, physical cell-cell interactions with surroundings, and gene expression readouts relating to phagocytosis and cytokine signaling. Each of these domains offers a window onto microglia function, and high-resolution confocal microscopy has long been a workhorse technique to visualize all three. A comprehensive view of microglia function requires both high-fidelity quantification with 3D resolution and colocalization of microglia with functional proteins such as those related to phagocytosis and with nearby structures such as synapses. Accordingly, a number of analytical tools have been developed to measure these features. However, existing open-source options lack either colocalization or 3D capability, while commercial solutions can be costly. Here, we sought to develop an open-source solution that addresses each of these limitations. PolyMorph3D is a MATLAB-based program capable of yielding individual cell-level data of microglia morphology and overlap with up to 4 other sources, all in 3D. The pipeline can be used effectively in mouse tissue and in human postmortem brain, thereby offering a flexible, low cost, and high-fidelity solution for the analysis of microglial morphology and function.
